blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — combined oral contraceptive missed-pill teaching
stem: A client using a combined oral contraceptive realizes that one hormonally active pill should have been taken 30 hours ago. Which instruction is most consistent with current CDC guidance?

options.A: Take the missed hormonal pill as soon as possible, continue the remaining pills at the usual time, and no additional contraceptive protection is routinely needed.
options.B: Discard the missed hormonal pill, continue with the next scheduled pill, and use a barrier method for the next 7 consecutive days.
options.C: Take the missed hormonal pill now, discard the rest of the current pack, and begin a new pack the following day to restore contraceptive protection.
options.D: Wait until the next scheduled dose, take two extra hormonal pills at that time, and use emergency contraception regardless of cycle timing.

rationale: CDC U.S. Selected Practice Recommendations state that when one hormonally active combined oral contraceptive pill has been missed for 24 to less than 48 hours, the client should take the missed pill as soon as possible and continue the remaining pills at the usual time, even if this results in two pills being taken on the same day. No additional contraceptive protection is needed. Therefore A is the best answer. B adds unnecessary backup and discards the missed pill, C unnecessarily restarts the pack, and D adds an unsupported extra-pill and routine emergency-contraception plan.
educational_objective: For one hormonally active combined oral contraceptive pill missed for 24 to less than 48 hours, take the missed pill as soon as possible, continue the remaining pills at the usual time, and recognize that routine backup contraception is not needed.

candidate_reasons_resolved: Removed isolated absolute-word distractors and rewrote all alternatives as complete missed-pill management plans.
Added the exact 30-hour delay so the one-pill 24-to-<48-hour CDC pathway is unambiguous.
Included the no-backup recommendation in the keyed plan to test complete guideline application rather than partial recall.
audit_note: Independent adversarial review confirms A uniquely matches CDC Figure 1 for one hormonally active pill missed 24 to <48 hours. B discards the missed pill and adds unnecessary backup, C unnecessarily restarts the pack, and D invents an unsupported dosing and routine emergency-contraception plan. No second defensible answer or material cueing remains.
